messages:
Kai: quick dump from prod canary: noticed steady RSS growth on long-context (>=32k) workloads, seems correlated with KV cache allocations not being reclaimed

Kai: pprof heap: top objects are kv_block (58%), small_chunk (22%), kv_meta (10%) — a lot of tiny allocations remaining live

Kai: sample snippet:
```
(pprof) top5
58.23%  58.23%  kv_block_alloc
22.10%  80.33%  small_chunk_malloc
10.12%  90.45%  kv_meta
```

Nina: ugh, sounds like fragmentation not leak. Are these slab-backed blocks or malloced per-kv-entry?

Kai: currently use hybrid: slab for larger blocks (>8k), fallback to sized alloc for <8k. Workload has many ~1.5k KV entries at long sequence caching -> lot of small tails

Devin: is this the same path where kernel selection tries to pack IO/GPUs? could batching heuristics be causing more partial KV writebacks (i.e., partial pages pinned longer)?

Kai: good point — batch coalescing can prolong KV lifetime because we keep prefix caches pinned until worker flush. Saw correlation between long alive requests and higher small_chunk counts

Maria: would adopting a different allocator (buddy vs slab vs jemalloc arenas) help? buddy with 4k granularity might reduce fragmentation for those 1.5k items by grouping. But risk: internal waste for large entries

Devin: let's not flip allocator wholesale. Two lower-risk knobs: increase slab bucket for small_chunk from 2k -> 4k (reduces number of buckets), or change block size to 16k to encourage fewer allocations and enable local compaction

Nina: 16k block size seems heavy for lots of small entries; but if we also enable free-list coalescing and a periodic compactor we could reclaim internal holes. Do we have cheap compaction story?

Kai: prototype compactor idea: background pass that finds adjacent free small_chunks within same block and coalesces them into larger free spans, run when load < 20%. Implementation sketch:
```
for block in blocks:
  if block.free_ratio > 0.3 and cpu_idle():
    scan_and_coalesce(block)
```

Kai: compaction metrics from a simulation (50k ops, 40% small entries): peak RSS down ~12%, tail latency hit negligible when scheduled off-peak

Maria: simulation looks promising. What's the cost to code? Also need correctness under concurrent access -> need lock-free handoff or epoch-based reclamation

Devin: another idea: prefix-aware eviction. Right now eviction is LRU on KV entry. If we detect that many small entries are contiguous in a block, evict them as a group to create larger free spans faster

Nina: +1 for group-eviction. But need to ensure it doesn't worsen user-facing miss rates. Could be combined with model-aware hints (e.g., don't group-evict hot prefixes)

Kai: plan proposal: 1) enable 4k min-chunk bucket (flags: --kv-min-chunk=4096) 2) add background block coalescer behind a config flag (--kv-compactor-enabled) 3) add group-eviction heuristic that prefers contiguous spans

Devin: safety: feature-gate compactor and run on canaries (dedicated small fleet) + add SLO guard to kill compactor if tail P99 increases by >5%

Kai: I ran a quick canary binary with compactor off and min-chunk=4096 on prod-candidate cluster for 6h: mean RSS down 6%, no latency regression. Will push compactor prototype to my branch tomorrow

Maria: good. Also add telemetry: per-block fragmentation ratio, compaction runs, compaction time, p99 before/after compaction. Put dashboards in console (per-route KV fragmentation view)

sre-bot: noted: create an incident playbook entry if compactor causes >10% increase in p99 or >3% error-rate spike

ci-bot: @Kai CI build queued for branch kv/compactor-proto #4571

Nina: edge case: background compaction under memory pressure could thrash. Add backoff and abort if RSS > threshold (e.g., 0.85 * container_mem_limit)

Devin: also test with long-context RLHF sim (64k tokens) - those allocate long KVs and are the main repro for this. Please include kernel selection interplay test where batching keeps prefix caches alive

Kai: will add tests: 1) microbench for small chunk churn, 2) integration with long-context workload, 3) canary rollout plan + SLO gating

Maria: timeline?

Kai: proto branch tomorrow, internal review by Thu, canary next week if review passes. I'll add detailed changelog and config flags in PR

Devin: smooth. Once we have metrics + dashboard we'll decide whether to raise default min-chunk or enable compactor by default

Kai: final note — we should document tradeoffs in runtime docs: memory growth vs internal waste vs compaction CPU cost. I'll draft short RFC after the prototype

Maria: thanks everyone. @Devin @Nina please help review compactor concurrency bits when Kai posts PR :thumbsup:
